result.definitions: D=Pred(a)\Pred(b); T=Max(D); U=Min{z:b<z and z||a}; R=reverse nonneutral endpoint remainder
result.theorem: R equals the union of events {b<t} over t in T and {u<a} over u in U; |T|,|U|<=2; every t is a Hasse predecessor of a and every u a Hasse successor of b.
result.majority_late_no_descent: If b prec_* a and no canonical strict span descent occurs, then R>E/3 while every canonical atom is <E/3, hence at least two channels are active. In the strict nested case, U=empty forces |T|=2, the double-predecessor Hasse fan.
result.lead_integration: The lead r12 crossed-neighborhood identity is the specialization with the forward blocker set empty (Q=E). Without crossed successor nesting, R remains bounded by four canonical Hasse channels.
result.partner_integration: The partner chain-D reverse branching is recovered when |T|=1. This run removes the chain hypothesis and identifies the exact successor-free failure state |T|=2,U=empty.

decisive_counterexample_to_shortcut.claim_refuted: width three plus connected comparability and incomparability graphs rules out the double-predecessor successor-free local state
decisive_counterexample_to_shortcut.note: This six-element poset is not a POS3 counterexample; it has balanced pairs. It only refutes the graph-connectivity shortcut.

next_obligation: In the series- and parallel-indecomposable minimal hard core, show that canonical successor continuation cannot terminate in a double-predecessor fan without a balanced pair, strict majority-span descent, width-four antichain, or excluded autonomous nonchain. Graph connectivity alone is insufficient.
